classification.difficultyReason: Compare coefficients, select the fourth-quadrant auxiliary angle and solve the resulting negative sine equation on the stated domain.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express $\sin x-\sqrt{3}\cos x$ in the form $C\sin(x+\beta)$, where $C>0$ and $0<\beta<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sin x-\sqrt{3}\cos x&=C\sin x\cos\beta+C\cos x\sin\beta\\C\cos\beta&=1\\C\sin\beta&=-\sqrt{3}\\C^2(\cos^2\beta+\sin^2\beta)&=1^2+(-\sqrt{3})^2\\C&=2\quad(C>0)\\\tan\beta&=-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$$
Since $\cos\beta>0$ and $\sin\beta<0$, $\beta$ is in quadrant IV.
$$\begin{aligned}\beta&=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{5\pi}{3}\\\sin x-\sqrt{3}\cos x&=2\sin\left(x+\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence solve $\sin x-\sqrt{3}\cos x=-1$, for $0\le x<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}2\sin\left(x+\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)&=-1\\\sin\left(x+\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)&=-\frac12\end{aligned}$$
The transformed domain is $\frac{5\pi}{3}\le x+\frac{5\pi}{3}<\frac{11\pi}{3}$.
$$\begin{aligned}x+\frac{5\pi}{3}&=\frac{11\pi}{6}\text{ or }\frac{19\pi}{6}\\x&=\frac{\pi}{6}\text{ or }\frac{3\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$$
